thread:
maya: FYI customer reported logins all started failing ~10:00 UTC after they said they rotated their IdP keystore earlier this morning. Getting 403s at our ACS.

maya: Customer (Acme Corp) says users see "Your account cannot be accessed (403)" right after SAML POST. They did a key rotation and published new metadata.

maya: Pasted their error from our logs: `ERROR auth.saml: SAML_RESPONSE_INVALID recipient_mismatch=1 cert_fingerprint_unknown=1`

raj: Can you drop the raw Assertion/Response (redacted) or at least the Recipient and SubjectConfirmation data? Need to see exact ACS URL in the assertion.

maya: Copied snippet (redacted):
```
<SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs" NotOnOrAfter="2024-04-05T10:05:00Z"/>
```

maya: Our SP ACS is configured as `https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs/` (note trailing slash). Customer's Assertion recipient lacks trailing slash. They rotated keys just before this started.

lina: Recipient mismatch will cause `403 SAML_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH` on our side. But logs also show `cert_fingerprint_unknown` which means the signing cert in the Response didn't match any cert we have for that IdP. Did the metadata update propagate to our metadata cache?

idp-sync-bot: metadata-sync: Acme-IdP metadata fetch succeeded 1712345600 -> certs updated, cache-version=20240405-1

raj: Bot says metadata updated, but it's possible the Response was signed with the old key during a staggered rollout. We should support checking both the old and new certs for a short window.

lina: Agree. For this customer we can temporarily accept either cert while they finish rotating. But first step: confirm Customer has the correct Assertion Recipient (or we normalize trailing slash).

maya: Asked customer to 1) confirm their SP entity/ACS in the IdP config and 2) re-generate one signed assertion with the new cert and send it to us (redacted) for repro. Provided a curl example to reproduce locally: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs/ \
  -F 'SAMLResponse=<BASE64_SIGNED_RESPONSE>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data'
```

maya: Customer replied with a samltrace export showing Response signed with old cert and Recipient without trailing slash. They said they expected metadata refresh to update SP config in IdP but their IdP applies ACS changes separate from certs (ugh).

raj: Ok reproduce steps work. When I POST the customer's Response signed with old cert, our code path rejects (recipient mismatch + unknown cert). I then re-post with new cert signature and Recipient with trailing slash and it succeeds.

lina: Proposed immediate actions: (1) Notify customer to reconfigure Acme IdP to use ACS `https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs/` (trailing slash) or allow both variants. (2) We’ll add a short window (48h) tolerance to check both old/new certs when metadata updates occur. (3) Create follow-up RFC to normalize ACS URL comparisons (strip trailing slash) but only after product/security sign-off.

maya: Customer is ok doing the quick fix (update ACS). They're concerned about users in middle of rotation — asked for mitigation.

raj: For mitigation we can temporarily mark their IdP entry as "accept-legacy-cert" in support tooling which will check both certs. I can flip it on for 24-48h. I'll also monitor logs for `SAML_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH` and `cert_fingerprint_unknown` spikes.

lina: I'll draft the RFC for normalization and a safe rollback plan. Also raising a security review because loosening checks affects trust model; must be explicit that acceptance window is temporary and audited.

maya: Done: enabled accept-legacy-cert for acme-corp for 36h. Customer reports SSO working for a handful of test users.

maya: Notes for postmortem: customer rotated keys and updated metadata, but IdP sent signed Responses with old key for some users AND had ACS configured without trailing slash. Two independent mismatches caused blanket 403. Recommend documenting recommended IdP rollout steps and adding an admin checklist.

raj: I'll add a short dashboard alert for `SAML_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH` spikes so support gets early warning next time.

lina: Filing security-approved exception for this maint window and adding follow-ups: RFC for URL normalization, metadata-caching verification improvements, and support playbook entry.

maya: Closing this thread. Customer SSO restored; will follow up on RFC and playbook."
